newsitem.title: ZAIRE: Hutu refugees dying in east Zaire forest - UNHCR.
newsitem.headline: Hutu refugees dying in east Zaire forest - UNHCR.

text.p: Hutu refugees too weak to flee eastern Zaire camps are dying from disease and hunger as thousands more hide in nearby forests, the U.N. refugee agency said on Wednesday.
"We got a report that 35 people have died within three days," said United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees representative Craig Sanders after a visit to the Tingi Tingi and Amisi camps.
U.N. agencies on Wednesday supplied biscuits and blankets to the camps, which may be used as staging posts for the repatriation of the refugees to their homes in Rwanda and Burundi.
Around 170,000 refugees fled Tingi Tingi before it was captured on February 1 by rebels fighting to overthrow Zaire's government.

While rebels have now moved on towards their stated target of Kisangani, 250 km (160 miles) to the northwest, many of the refugees have fled towards Ubundu on the Zaire river 100 km (60 miles) south of Kisangani.

People in Amisi camp say that over 1,000 are staying there, while in the immediate vicintiy of Tingi Tingi there are over 500 refugees. Refugees and local people say thousands more remain hidden in the dense forest that cloaks the region.
The UNHCR plans to encourage people to emerge from the forest and then return them home.
"Our presence here will be a major encouragement to refugees to return," said Sanders.

The bulk of the refugees are Rwandan Hutus who fled camps further west after the advance of the Tutsi-led rebel force and live in fear of reprisals for the 1994 genocide of 800,000 Tutsis and Hutu moderates.
